notes.decision: Translated as 'the work' — Lyc ⲡⲣ̄- (article cluster) + ⲍⲱⲃ (= ϩⲱⲃ 'work,' already in glossary). The verbal idiom ⲣ̄-ⲡⲣ̄ⲍⲱⲃ 'do the work' is the controlling phrase of the kephalaion (also at lines 15, 22).

Translated tentatively as 'a portion / your portion.' The lexeme is unusual; appears here at line 3 as 'let a ⲍⲏⲣ become in your life' and at line 26 as 'your toil shall be reckoned to your ⲍⲏⲣ' — semantic field of 'share, account, recompense.' Possible Lyc reflex relating to ⲡⲱⲣⲱ 'lot' or a specific Manichaean technical term for the disciple's accumulated merit/account before the Apostle. Confidence moderate. Flagged for parallel attestations in subsequent kephalaia.

Translated as 'waver' based on context: line 4 'even though others ⲃⲁϣⲃⲉϣ' (others' negative behavior) parallels line 5 'do not ⲃⲁϣⲃⲉϣ' (warning to disciple). The reduplicated form likely related to ⲡⲱϣⲡⲱϣ 'split, divide' or a deficiency-verb yielding 'waver, be divided in heart, be lax.' Pairs with Greek παραιτεῖσθαι 'refuse, decline' as parallel negative behaviors to avoid. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Translated as 'refuse / decline' from Greek παραιτεῖσθαι 'beg off, decline, refuse.' The construction ⲡⲁⲣⲉⲧⲓ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϥ 'refuse himself' fits the moral exhortation: do not beg off from the work. Standard Greek loanword in Coptic.

Left as transliterated 'paraphon' — obscure Greek loanword in series ⲉⲁⲩ-ⲡⲟⲣⲟ-ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲫⲟⲛ ('glory-kingship-X') as honors of the proclaimer. Possible candidates: παρρησία 'boldness/free-speech' (corrupted spelling), παράφορον 'mark of distinction,' or παράκλησις 'exhortation.' Cannot identify with confidence; flagged for parallels.

Translated 'folds himself by himself, and turns himself by himself' — describing the brother of righteous heart who withdraws inward and remains alone. ⲁⲗϥ from ⲱⲗϥ̄ 'fold, bend' (cf. Crum); ⲕⲁⲧϥ̄ from ⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'turn.' The double ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉϥ 'alone' emphasizes solitary withdrawal — contrasted with the active proclamation that builds the Church.

'But the man himself who speaks, who commands' — pivot from the previous case (one who builds with his word and has no sin) to the contrasting case: the man who speaks and commands but does not himself do the work. The grammatical emphasis ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϥ 'himself' marks the personal accountability of the speaker.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲣⲍⲱⲃ ⲉϩⲁⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲃⲉ
notes.decision: 'The work shall stand entirely upon him in the sin' — using the standard Coptic ⲱϩⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧ⸗ idiom 'stand on the feet of' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast'). The work-burden falls back upon the speaker who fails to act. ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲃⲉ likely Lyc article cluster + 'sin' rather than a possessive form.

'Your toil shall be reckoned to your portion' — using ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (in glossary) with directional ⲁ- 'to.' The construction parallels biblical-soteriological 'reckoning to one's account' (cf. Romans 4:3-5). The disciple's labor in church-building accrues to his ⲍⲏⲣ (portion/account/credit).

notes.decision: 'Let your power and your glory help me' — standard disciple's petition closing the kephalaion. The disciple acknowledges that the proclaimer's work cannot succeed without the Apostle's continued power (ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ) and glory (ⲉⲁⲩ) standing behind him. ⲣ̄ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲉⲓ from Greek βοηθέω 'help, aid.'
